*   **Time Complexity:** Rendering time is proportional to $N \cdot N_s \cdot 16 \cdot 16$ for the volume rendering step, plus the cost of the 2D neural renderer for upsampling to the final resolution [S1].

The claim states that rendering time is proportional to $N$ (number of entities), $N_s$ (number of sample points), and $16^2$ (resolution of the feature image, 16x16), plus the cost of 2D neural rendering. The evidence supports this: [S1] defines $N$ as the number of entities, $N_s$ as the number of sample points (value 64), and explicitly states that feature images are rendered at resolution $16^2$ (16x16) for efficiency before being upsampled via 2D neural rendering. The volume rendering step involves evaluating the feature field for each of the $N$ entities at each of the $N_s$ sample points for each pixel in the $16^2$ grid, making the complexity proportional to these factors.
